```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 140)
library(ontophylo)
```

This workflow estimates mapped change rates for a combined character or an
anatomical group. Each character is first fitted and mapped separately. For each
map replicate, its changes are counted on each branch; counts are summed across
the selected characters and divided by branch duration. Marginal rates average
these branch rates across the sampled lineages present at each age.

The branch-specific estimator retains Sergei Tarasov's Hymenoptera functions.
`branch_rate_pipeline()` adds group handling, normalization, predefined branch
comparisons and a consistent final result. It does not require discretizing
histories or constructing a stacked-state map.

## Pipeline and function names

The diagram names the public entry points. Internally, the higher-order wrapper
summarizes already computed rate samples, so it does not repeat amalgamation.
`branch_rate_thru_time_Multi()` calls `branch_rate_thru_time()` separately for
each replicate before calculating uncertainty.

| Function | Role |
|:--|:--|
| `fit_models()` | Fit and compare candidate Q models per character. |
| `paramo_stm()` | Sample conditional stochastic histories, optionally in batches on disk. |
| `read_stm()` | Load complete selections of maps from the mapping result. |
| `count_branch_changes()` | Count changes on each branch of one original map. |
| `get_branch_rate_sample_smaps()` | Obtain branch-rate samples for one character. |
| `ama_branches_multi_char()` | Sum branch rates across characters within each replicate. |
| `summarize_branch_rates()` | Summarize a single character across its maps. |
| `summarize_branch_rates_multi()` | Summarize a combined character across its maps. |
| `branch_rate_thru_time()` | Marginalize one branch-rate vector through time. |
| `branch_rate_thru_time_Multi()` | Marginalize all replicates and summarize the curves. |
| `branch_rates()` | Return branch and marginal results for one combined character. |
| `branch_rate_pipeline()` | Run selected anatomical groups, normalization and comparisons. |
| `branch_rate_contrast()` | Compare two predefined, disjoint branch sets within each replicate. |
| `plot_branch_colored_tree()` | Display branch values on a tree. |
| `plot_marginal_rates()` | Display a marginal curve with pointwise map intervals. |

## Fit models and sample histories

The following small example is executable. The rows identify taxa, and each
column is a separate binary character. In this example all characters are
variable; inspect the fitting and mapping status tables before analyzing a new
dataset. Failed or skipped characters must not disappear silently.

```{r fit-models}
tree <- ape::read.tree(text =
  "(((a:1,b:1):1,(c:1,d:1):1):1,((e:1,f:1):1,(g:1,h:1):1):1);")
characters <- cbind(
  char1 = c("0", "0", "0", "0", "1", "1", "1", "1"),
  char2 = c("0", "0", "1", "1", "0", "0", "1", "1"),
  char3 = c("1", "1", "0", "0", "0", "0", "1", "1"))
rownames(characters) <- tree$tip.label

fits <- fit_models(tree, characters, models = c("ER", "SYM", "ARD"),
                    root_p = "equal", criterion = "AICc", nstarts = 0,
                    seed = 101, on_error = "stop")
fits$status
fits$characters$char1$model_table

mapped <- paramo_stm(fits, n_stm = 25, batch_size = 10,
                      seed = 102, on_error = "stop")
mapped$status
maps <- read_stm(mapped)
names(maps)
```

The same root setting is carried from fitting to mapping. Binary ER and SYM
represent the same model and are not fitted twice. Model selection and fixed-Q
mapping do not propagate uncertainty in Q or model choice into the subsequent
mapping intervals. See the fitting help pages for custom Q index matrices,
missing and ambiguous observations, and checkpoint/resumption settings.

If maps were generated elsewhere, supply the same structure directly:
`list(char1 = maps_for_char1, char2 = maps_for_char2)`. For example,
`phytools::make.simmap()` supplies each character's map list. These must be the
original maps, before discretization or stacked-state amalgamation.

## One call from maps to final outputs

```{r high-order-wrapper}
groups <- list(combined = names(maps), region_A = c("char1", "char2"),
                region_B = c("char2", "char3"))
result <- branch_rate_pipeline(maps, groups = groups, normalize = "characters",
                                time_points = seq(3, 0, by = -0.1),
                                time_scale = "age")
result$group_summary
head(result$branch_summary)
head(result$marginal_summary)

combined <- result$groups$combined
dim(combined$rate_samples)       # branches x map replicates
dim(combined$marginal_samples)   # ages x map replicates
```

The mapping result can also be passed directly. This reads one character's
branch-count samples at a time and supports disk-backed or count-only runs:

```{r direct-mapping-result}
direct <- branch_rate_pipeline(mapped, groups, normalize = "characters",
                                time_points = seq(3, 0, by = -0.1),
                                time_scale = "age")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(direct$branch_summary, result$branch_summary)))
```

Count-only storage is sufficient for branch-specific and marginal rates, but
cannot reproduce the transition times required by stacked-map analyses.

`region_A` and `region_B` overlap in `char2`. They are separate results; they
are never summed to produce the combined group. The combined group explicitly
contains the three unique characters. A named list returned by `RAC_query()`
can be used as `groups` when all of its character IDs occur in `maps`.

With `normalize = "none"`, rates are total character changes per time unit.
With `normalize = "characters"`, samples, means, SDs and interval bounds are
all divided by the number of characters in their group. This makes units
comparable across differently sized groups; it does not correct differences
in state spaces or data quality.

## Every lower-level function

For branch b, character c and map replicate m, let N be the reconstructed
number of changes and L the branch duration. The combined rate is

\[
r_{bm} = \frac{\sum_c N_{bcm}}{L_b}.
\]

This estimates a realized mapped change rate, rather than fitting a separate
Q matrix to each branch. Reversals are counted. Adjacent segments labelled
with the same state do not create a change.

```{r count-and-amalgamate}
counts <- count_branch_changes(maps$char1[[1]])
head(counts)

one_character <- get_branch_rate_sample_smaps(maps$char1)
head(one_character[[1]])

combined_samples <- ama_branches_multi_char(maps)
head(combined_samples[[1]])

single_mean <- summarize_branch_rates(maps$char1, stat = "mean")
combined_mean <- summarize_branch_rates_multi(maps, stat = "mean")
combined_bounds <- summarize_branch_rates_multi(maps, stat = "quantile",
                                                probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
head(single_mean)
head(combined_mean)
combined_bounds[, 1:4, drop = FALSE]
```

For one replicate, the marginal rate is the mean of the rates of branches
present at a specified age. The number of contributing branches is returned.
It is important to marginalize each replicate first: averaging branch-level
interval endpoints does not give the marginal interval.

```{r marginal-functions}
one_curve <- branch_rate_thru_time(tree, combined_samples[[1]],
                                   time_points = c(3, 2.5, 2, 1, 0),
                                   time_scale = "age")
one_curve

curves <- branch_rate_thru_time_Multi(tree, combined_samples,
                                      time_points = seq(3, 0, by = -0.1),
                                      time_scale = "age", return_samples = TRUE)
head(curves$summary)

one_combined_character <- branch_rates(maps, n_points = 31)
head(one_combined_character$branch_summary)
```

The default `time_scale = "root"` preserves the original interface: supplied
times are elapsed from the root. `time_scale = "age"` accepts ages before the
present. Returned `time` always means age before the present. At an internal
node, descendant branches contribute instead of their ancestor; at the present,
terminal branches contribute their limiting rates. Marginal reconstruction
requires a rooted ultrametric tree. Branch-only reconstruction is available
with `marginal = FALSE`.

## Predefined clade contrasts

Define focal and reference branches before examining inferred rates. The
example below compares the terminal branches of two named tip groups. It
illustrates the interface, rather than a biological hypothesis about this toy
dataset. A real clade comparison can include internal branches as well.

```{r clade-contrasts}
focal_tips <- match(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), tree$tip.label)
reference_tips <- match(c("e", "f", "g", "h"), tree$tip.label)
focal <- which(tree$edge[, 2] %in% focal_tips)
reference <- which(tree$edge[, 2] %in% reference_tips)
comparison <- branch_rate_contrast(combined, focal, reference)
comparison$summary
comparison$fraction_focal_greater

comparisons <- list(left_vs_right = list(focal = focal, reference = reference))
with_contrasts <- branch_rate_pipeline(maps, groups,
                                       normalize = "characters", contrasts = comparisons)
with_contrasts$contrasts$combined$left_vs_right$summary
```

By default, rates within each branch set are weighted by branch duration.
The resulting value is total mapped changes divided by total lineage time.
`weighting = "equal"` instead treats branches equally. Differences and ratios
are calculated within each replicate and then summarized. If a reference rate
is zero, its ratio is undefined and this is reported explicitly; differences
remain available. There is no automatic pseudocount.

**`fraction_focal_greater` is not a p-value.** The intervals condition on the
mapping model. They are not automatically calibrated confidence intervals for
generating rate ratios, and selecting high-rate branches from the same result
would make a subsequent contrast circular.

## Plot the results

```{r branch-plot, fig.cap="Combined-character branch rates in the example, expressed per character per tree time unit."}
plot_branch_colored_tree(combined$tree, combined$branch_summary$mean,
                         legend_title = "Rate per character", edge.width = 3,
                         cex = 0.8)
```

```{r marginal-plot, fig.cap="Marginal rates over sampled lineages. Shading is the pointwise central 95% interval across map replicates, conditional on the fitted models and tree."}
plot_marginal_rates(combined$marginal_summary,
                     ylab = "Mapped changes per character per time unit")
```

## Rate-heterogeneity validation

The reproducible benchmark is installed with the package in
`validation/branch-rates`. It uses the previously specified 100-tip tree with
a root age of 150 Ma. The focal 45-tip clade contains 76 whole branches whose
parent age is at most 50 Ma; 70 other young branches serve as the reference.
Branches crossing 50 Ma retain the baseline rate throughout.

There are 30 independently simulated datasets in each of two conditions, with
20 binary characters per dataset and equal root-state frequencies:

* **Homogeneous control:** q = 0.002 per Myr on every branch.
* **Accelerated clade:** q = 0.020 on focal young branches, and 0.002 elsewhere.

For this downstream benchmark, each character is reconstructed under its own
homogeneous ER model fitted with `phytools::fitMk()`, followed by 50 conditional
maps from `phytools::make.simmap()`. The same mapping assumptions are used for
both conditions. This independent fitting route isolates the downstream
estimator; the executable example above separately tests the package's
`fit_models()` and `paramo_stm()` interface.

The simulator uses the exact symmetric-binary construction: Poisson event
counts, uniformly distributed event times conditional on the count, and state
flips inherited along the tree. Its event means and endpoint-state frequencies
are checked against the analytic Mk distribution. True histories are retained
to distinguish simulation/accounting correctness from inference using only tip
observations. All characters, including invariant tip patterns, are retained in
the benchmark. No histories are selected for favourable recovery. Unidentified
high-rate fitting plateaus stop a run with saved diagnostics rather than
triggering silent character removal.

```{r validation-summary, echo=FALSE}
summary_file <- system.file("validation", "branch-rates", "results",
                            "scenario-summary.csv", package = "ontophylo")
stopifnot(nzchar(summary_file))
validation <- read.csv(summary_file)
knitr::kable(validation, digits = 3,
              col.names = c("Condition", "Datasets", "Median AUC", "Median ratio",
                              "Interval excludes equal rates", "Interval covers true ratio"))
```

```{r validation-figure, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Validation on the fixed 100-tip tree. Each point represents one independently simulated character dataset. AUC describes discrimination between focal and reference young branches; it is not a branch-wise significance test."}
figure <- system.file("validation", "branch-rates", "results",
                      "rate-recovery.png", package = "ontophylo")
stopifnot(nzchar(figure))
knitr::include_graphics(figure)
```

The validation report separates branch-ranking discrimination, recovered fold
change, coverage of the generating ratio, and the frequency with which the
conditional mapping interval excludes equal rates under the homogeneous
control. These are distinct properties. Good localization can coexist with
substantial attenuation of the generating fold increase.

In the homogeneous control, the conditional interval excluded equal rates in
`r validation$Excludes_equal[1]` datasets. Under a true ten-fold acceleration,
the median inferred ratio was `r round(validation$Median_ratio[2], 2)` and the
median AUC was `r round(validation$Median_AUC[2], 3)`; the interval covered the
generating ratio in `r validation$Covers_true_ratio[2]` datasets. Thus the
method localized the strong accelerated regime in this design, but its
conditional mapping intervals are unsuitable as nominal 5% tests of underlying
rate heterogeneity or as calibrated intervals for the generating fold change.

The fixed-tree benchmark does not establish robustness to incomplete taxon
sampling, phylogenetic error or polytomies. Nor does it measure adaptation or
provide a calibrated discovery test for unknown accelerated branches. The
number of simulated datasets is too small to establish precise tail error
rates; raw results and their counts are supplied for interpretation.

To rerun the benchmark, copy its installed directory into a writable folder
and run `Rscript --vanilla run-validation.R`. Optional arguments specify the
output directory, datasets per condition and maps per character. Environment
variables `ONTO_FIRST_DATASET` and `ONTO_LAST_DATASET` allow disjoint chunks;
seeds are independent of worker scheduling and completed datasets are reused.

## Input and uncertainty checks

* All characters must share the tree, tip labels, edge order, branch lengths
  and map sample size. Edge order is checked, not silently inferred.
* Branch lengths and mapped segment durations must be positive. Segment
  durations must sum to their corresponding branch length.
* Map replicate identities are retained through amalgamation, normalization,
  comparisons and marginalization. Independently sampled character histories
  can be paired by position; dependent characters require joint draws.
* Fixed-Q mapping intervals exclude uncertainty in fitted Q, model choice,
  topology, dating and taxon sampling. A larger number of maps reduces Monte
  Carlo error but does not remove those limitations.
